name: Dark eyeliner to make iris pop
lead: Dark eyeliner to make the iris pop is a makeup practice in which dark liner is applied along the lash line, and sometimes the waterline, to increase contrast with the iris. Practitioners say the dark frame makes eye colour look brighter and the eyes look more defined.[1]

Eyeliner comes as liquid, gel, kohl, wax or powder pencils, cake and felt-tip formats; tight lining along the waterline is described as making lashes look longer and fuller, and liner in general is used to define the eyes and make them look wider or smaller.[1] The contrast idea parallels simultaneous contrast in vision science, in which surrounding colours and brightness change how an adjacent area is perceived.[2]
No published study of dark liner and perceived iris colour was identified.
infobox: Liquid, gel, kohl, wax or powder pencil[1]
Upper lash line, tight lining, winged liner[1]

paras: The idea is that a dark frame around the eye heightens the apparent brightness of the iris. This is a practitioner claim. Eyeliner itself has a long history: Wikipedia describes dark lines around the eyes in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia, with kohl made from materials such as copper ore, antimony and galena, and a tomb in Thebes from the 15th century BC showing men and women wearing it.[1]

Liquid liner is opaque and applied with a fine brush for sharp lines, often winged, and is usually kept to the upper lash line. Wax-based pencils are soft and cheap, kohl is a soft matte powder that smudges easily, gel liner allows precise brush application, and felt-tip liners need no sharpening.[1]

Liner can go above the upper lashes, below the lower lashes, or on the waterline; tight lining places it near the lashes, and waterproof formulas are recommended for placement close to the eye's surface.[1] Common pigments include black iron oxides with smaller amounts of titanium dioxide and Prussian blue.[1]

sections.h: Why contrast changes how colour looks
paras: Simultaneous contrast describes how a surrounding colour or brightness changes the perceived look of an adjacent area; the same gray patch can look lighter or darker depending on its background, and the strength depends on factors such as the size of the surrounding field and the luminance difference.[2] Practitioners apply the same reasoning to the iris, with dark liner as the surround.

timeline.event: A tomb in Thebes shows men and women wearing kohl.[1]
Liquid liner popularised for bold lines by designers such as Mary Quant.[1]

card.summary: Dark liner around the eye to contrast the iris and make its color look brighter; a makeup tip with no studies.
card.note: No published studies found; liner contacts the eye area.

quick.overview:
Dark eyeliner along the lash line is used to frame the eye so the iris color looks stronger.

The claim comes from makeup practice, and no research on this specific effect was found.
quick.mechanism: A dark border is said to increase local contrast, making the iris seem lighter or more saturated.
quick.risks: General eyeliner cautions apply, such as irritation or infection from contaminated products; sources reviewed give no specific data.

chain: Dark liner placed along lash line
Iris appears brighter and more saturated by contrast
angle.text: People line the upper lash line, or tight-line the waterline, so a dark border frames the iris. Practitioners say this makes pale or coloured eyes stand out more.
